title: Trigonometric Values of Special Angles
seo_title: Precalculus Trigonometric Values of Special Angles Worksheets (TEKS P.2P, P.4A, P.4E)
standard_text: P.2P determine the values of the trigonometric functions at the special angles and relate them in mathematical and real-world problems; P.4A determine the relationship between the unit circle and the definition of a periodic function to evaluate trigonometric functions in mathematical and real-world problems; P.4E determine the value of trigonometric ratios of angles and solve problems involving trigonometric ratios in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets for Texas TEKS P.2P, P.4A and P.4E: exact trig values of special angles, unit circle points, reciprocal functions and ratios from a quadrant. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The point at angle θ on the unit circle is (cos θ, sin θ).
key_sub: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine: the positive ratios in Quadrants I to IV.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • On the unit circle, the point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ), and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.
  • Special angles: 30° (π/6), 45° (π/4), 60° (π/3) and their reference angles in every quadrant.
  • Signs: All positive in Quadrant I, Sine in II, Tangent in III, Cosine in IV.
  • csc θ = 1 ÷ sin θ, sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ, cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

Examples

Example

cos 240°

Reference angle 60°

Quadrant III: cosine is negative

Answer: −12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong signCheck the quadrant first.
Swapping sine and cosineThe x-coordinate is cosine.
Flipping the wrong ratiosec goes with cos, csc goes with sin.

items.q: If cos θ = 1213 and θ is in Quadrant I, what is cot θ?
